flags.harmony: You'd rather keep the peace than argue
flags.smallcircle: You're loyal to a small, close circle (and need alone time to recharge)
flags.anxious: You sometimes need reassurance in close friendships
flags.lastminute: You tend to leave things to the last minute
flags.tradition: You care a lot about rules and doing what's expected
flags.quiet: When you're stressed, you go quiet and handle it yourself

questions.text: What's the earliest memory you have? Describe it like a little scene.
questions.hint: Where were you, who was there, and how did it feel?

questions.text: When you picture the home you grew up in, the first feeling that comes up is…
What's a smell, sound, or song that instantly takes you back to being a kid?
What did you love to play or pretend when you were little?
questions.hint: Games, made-up worlds, toys, characters, anything.

alt.intro: Your Mindprint showed a big imagination.
alt.text: Where did it come from? What did your imagination get up to when you were little (pretend games, made-up worlds, stories)?

questions.text: When I was little, I wanted to be ___ when I grew up, because ___.
How loud or quiet was your house, usually?
Describe a normal weeknight evening at home when you were about eight.
questions.hint: Dinner, TV, homework, who was around…

questions.text: Who did you grow up living with?
options: I split time between two homes

questions.text: Was your family more of a "talk about feelings" family or a "keep it to yourself" family?
options: We talked about pretty much everything
We mostly didn't talk about them

questions.text: What's one thing about the home you grew up in that you'd want in your own home someday?
As a kid, did you get good at "reading the room" at home? What did you notice?
questions.hint: Like picking up on someone's mood when they walked in.

questions.text: How did your parents or guardians show love?
options: Doing things for me (cooking, rides, help)
Encouraging me and cheering me on

questions.text: Think of a moment when you felt really loved as a kid. What happened?
In my family, "I love you" sounded like ___.
questions.hint: It could be the actual words, or something like "text me when you get there."

questions.text: How easy was it to go to a parent or guardian when you needed something?
Is there a way you show love now that you picked up from your family?
When the adults in your house disagreed, what usually happened?
options: It's different for different people in my family

questions.text: When there was tension at home, what was your role? Were you the peacekeeper, the one who spoke up, or the one who stayed out of it?

alt.intro: Earlier you said you'd rather keep the peace than argue. It was one of your strongest results.
alt.text: Where do you think you learned that? Was there someone at home who kept the peace, too?

questions.text: When you and a parent or guardian disagreed as a kid, you usually…
options: Gave in to keep the peace
Went quiet and let it pass
Tried to meet in the middle
It depended on who it was

alt.intro: This one ties back to how you handle conflict now.

questions.text: How did your family make up after an argument?
questions.hint: Saying sorry, a hug, a treat, just acting normal again, or not really at all.

questions.text: When people around me argued, the kid version of me wanted to ___.
How strict were the rules in your house?
What was a rule at home that you thought was totally unfair? Do you still think so?
When you messed up as a kid, what usually happened?
options: We had a calm talk about it
I got in trouble, then it was over
I felt like I'd let someone down
Not much. It got brushed off.

questions.text: What did your family expect of you growing up?
questions.hint: Grades, chores, behavior, helping out, anything.

alt.intro: Your results showed you care a lot about rules and doing what's expected.
alt.text: Whose expectations did you most want to live up to growing up, and what did they expect of you?

questions.text: What kind of praise meant the most to you as a kid, and who gave it?
As a kid, how much did criticism sting?
How did your family handle homework, chores, and deadlines?

alt.intro: You admitted you tend to leave things to the last minute (honestly, same as most people).
alt.text: Were you like that when you were little, too? How did your parents or guardians handle homework and deadlines?

questions.text: Where do you fall among the kids in your family?
If you have siblings (or cousins you grew up close to), what were you like together as kids? If not, what was it like being the only kid?
Which relative (a grandparent, aunt, uncle, or cousin) mattered most to you as a kid, and why?
questions.hint: Just their role is perfect. No names needed.

questions.text: Think of one parent or guardian. What's something you really admire about them?
questions.hint: "My mom," "my grandpa," or "my stepdad" is perfect. No names needed.

questions.text: Now think of another parent or guardian, if you have one. What do you admire about them?
questions.hint: If this doesn't apply to you, just tap Skip.

questions.text: Who are you more like?
What's a trait you got from your family that you're proud of? And one you're still figuring out?
One thing I wish my parents or guardians understood about me is ___.
What were you like in elementary school?
questions.hint: Shy, loud, teacher's pet, class clown, quiet artist…

questions.text: Who was your best friend as a kid, and what made them your person?

alt.intro: Mindprint says you'd rather have a few close people than a big crowd.
alt.text: Were you like that as a kid, too? Tell me about the friend (or friends) who were your people back then. No names needed.

questions.text: As a kid, where did you feel most like yourself?
options: At a grandparent's or relative's house
At practice, a club, or church

questions.text: How did you usually spend recess or free time?
options: With one or two close friends
On my own, and I liked it
It changed from year to year

questions.text: Did your family move, change schools, or go through any big changes while you were growing up? How did it feel at the time?
questions.hint: Share only what you want to.

questions.text: Overall, how stable and predictable did your childhood feel?
What's a family tradition you loved?
questions.hint: A holiday, a birthday thing, a weekend ritual, a special food…

questions.text: When you were upset as a kid, what helped you feel better?

alt.intro: Your results said that when things get stressful, you tend to go quiet and handle it on your own.
alt.text: Did you do that as a kid, too? When you were upset back then, what did you do, and what helped?

questions.text: When you were upset as a kid, who did you usually go to first?
options: A pet or a stuffed animal
No one. I kept it to myself.

questions.text: The thing that always made me feel safe as a kid was ___.
Is there anything from your childhood that you think shaped how you are in friendships now?

alt.intro: Mindprint picked up that you sometimes need a little reassurance in close friendships, like wondering whether someone's upset with you.
alt.text: Do you think anything from growing up shaped that? It's totally fine if you're not sure.

questions.text: If you raise kids someday, what's one thing you'd do the same as your parents or guardians, and one thing you'd do differently?
How much do you think your childhood shaped who you are now?
If you could tell your eight-year-old self one thing, what would it be?
